findings.message: Command Argument Injection via faulty LLM-supplied CLI arguments in shape_materialize.run()
findings.reason: A branch value reaches fixed git/gh argv, not a shell command. main calls checked_branch before any apply path; the branch alphabet and git check-ref-format --branch reject option/ref syntax. Push uses -- plus refs/heads/<branch>:refs/heads/<branch>. run checks the executable allowlist. No HTTP handler or privilege boundary exists on this CLI flow.
findings.status: source flow reviewed; service update pending

findings.message: Path Traversal via file content in shape_materialize._append_eol_block()
findings.reason: The alleged file-content path traversal has no file-content-derived destination: _append_eol_block uses target / ATTRIBUTES, where ATTRIBUTES is the fixed .gitattributes name. It writes only on the exact attributes collision and refuses disk symlinks, non-files and index-mode symlinks, including core.symlinks=false checkouts. Existing content is payload for with_eol_block, not a destination path.

findings.message: Path Traversal via faulty LLM-supplied CLI arguments in repo_shape.load_yaml()
findings.reason: load_yaml is an intentionally caller-selected local YAML reader. The traced CLI callers read --project, a fixed project.yaml below the selected repository root, or the selected local policy. Their explicit purpose is to validate an operator-selected filesystem tree. No network request, lower-privilege principal, confined-directory promise or privileged service is involved; an operator selecting a local input file is not a traversal across an authority boundary.

findings.message: Command Argument Injection via faulty LLM-supplied standard input in cli.run_child()
findings.reason: The org text entered on the terminal becomes the value after the fixed --org flag. run_child receives sys.executable followed by a known standard-owned Python script, using list argv and shell=False. The tools intentionally forward their documented options to that script, whose parser/validators own those values; stdin cannot select a program or add a shell fragment. This is a local CLI launcher, not an HTTP handler.
